segments.visible_description: The Draft card identifies the generated text as a starting point rather than finished copy.
segments.narration: Standing there with the real headlines, it landed: my draft didn't need a better writer.

segments.visible_description: At the NewsStand, a press worker and the heroine inspect the paper together under a magnifying glass.
segments.narration: It needed someone at the news desk, holding every confident line up to the light.

segments.visible_description: The newspaper asks the two exact verification questions in large type: Says who? Based on what?
The Claim card identifies the front-page statement as the thing that must be supported.
segments.narration: The machine had handed me a front page.

segments.visible_description: The newspaper returns with the explicit instruction to fact-check the front page before it runs under your byline.
segments.narration: My job was to fact-check it before it ran under my byline.

editorial_decision: Replace the 21-second newspaper hold with five narration-specific beats that move from the draft and real headlines to a human news-desk check, the two verification questions, the front-page claim and the byline responsibility.
